episodes.title: Monty Hall Problem Explained
episodes.description: Introduce statistics as a way of using observations and data to understand the world.

episodes.title: Introduction to Statistics
episodes.description: Statistics is humanity's best toolkit for distilling data about lots of stuff into reliable and comprehensible conclusions about everything from cookies to climate change.

episodes.title: Why Are There So Many Data Types?
episodes.description: A lot of planning and work go into collecting data to make sure that we can actually answer questions that interest us.

episodes.title: How to Identify Dependent & Independent Variables
episodes.description: Use dependent and independent variables to investigate cause, effect, and relationships in data.

episodes.title: What Kind of Data Do You Really Need?
episodes.description: Compare types of data and consider how measurement precision affects statistical analysis.

episodes.title: How to Organize Data in a Table
episodes.description: Explore how tables organize complex data into rows and columns to make information easier to understand.

episodes.title: What Is A Histogram?
episodes.description: Use histograms to examine distributions and understand the shape and characteristics of data.

episodes.title: How to Tell a Story with Data
episodes.description: Choose graph types and visual styles that communicate data clearly and honestly.

episodes.title: What is a Central Tendency?
episodes.description: Calculating a “central tendency”, like an average, is one of the most powerful ways we can meaningfully represent data.

episodes.title: Descriptive Statistics and Outliers
episodes.description: Examine typical data, unusual observations, and outliers to understand what a dataset may reveal.

episodes.title: Why Normal Distributions Are So Common
episodes.description: There’s a deep mathematical reason for this conspiracy of normal distributions everywhere, which has made waves throughout history: the central limit theorem.

episodes.title: What is the Empirical Rule?
episodes.description: Explore the empirical rule and how normal distributions help us interpret everyday data.

episodes.title: How to calculate Z-Scores
episodes.description: Standardize measurements to make comparisons across different units, scales, and distributions.

episodes.title: The guardrails of statistics: Confidence Intervals
episodes.description: Distributions and confidence intervals give us guardrails for measuring precisely how certain we ought to be in the statistics we do.

episodes.title: Types of Probability Distributions
episodes.description: Explore probability as a tool for understanding uncertainty, predicting outcomes, and managing risk.

episodes.title: What is Conditional Probability?
episodes.description: To disentangle what influences what, we need the tools to calculate complex probabilities.

episodes.title: How To Use Probability Distributions
episodes.description: Explore how sampling distributions and test statistics distinguish typical outcomes from unlikely ones.

episodes.title: What Is Hypothesis Testing?
episodes.description: Use the null hypothesis to approach uncertain conclusions with skepticism and make better-informed decisions.

episodes.title: P-value Hypothesis Testing
episodes.description: Examine errors in hypothesis testing and how understanding different mistakes can support better decisions.

episodes.title: One and Two Tailed Tests Explained
episodes.description: Compare one- and two-tailed tests when investigating differences between groups.

episodes.title: How to Run an Independent t-Test
episodes.description: Use independent t-tests to assess whether groups differ significantly.

episodes.title: How to Calculate Cohen’s D
episodes.description: Explore how comparing related groups can reveal statistical relationships and help distinguish meaningful results from chance.

episodes.title: What is a Chi-Square test?
episodes.description: And the chi-square test is exactly what we need in hypothesis testing to measure how well a model fits reality.

episodes.title: Chi Square: Independence and Homogeneity
episodes.description: The chi-square test of independence makes short work of uncovering the hidden relationships between two different categories or groups.

episodes.title: F Distribution and the Sum of Squares
episodes.description: Use the F statistic and F distribution to investigate variation within and between groups.

episodes.title: What is ANOVA?
episodes.description: Explore how analysis of variance investigates relationships between numerical measurements and groups.

episodes.title: How to Use Repeated Measures ANOVA
episodes.description: Use repeated-measures ANOVA to compare groups while controlling for variation between individual subjects.

episodes.title: Understanding the Correlation Coefficient
episodes.description: Correlation is everywhere, from parking issues when your favorite Swedish restaurant is packed to fertilizer usage and crop yields.

episodes.title: Intro to Simple Linear Regression
episodes.description: Explore how regression quantifies relationships between two measurements and when it can be used.

episodes.title: How to Use Multiple Linear Regression
episodes.description: This episode will show you how to do multiple linear regression, without falling into traps!

episodes.title: Which Stats Can You Trust?
episodes.description: Examine ethical uses of statistics and learn to question misleading data and statistical claims.
